summary: Intermittent dedicated-pool throughput collapse correlated with silent tenant burst and autoscaler sensitivity
description: Issue summary: BrightCompose reports repeated mid-window throughput collapses for their dedicated pool. Impact: customer p99 latency increased from 80ms to 2.3s and overall throughput dropped ~42% for 5-15 minute windows several times across the last 48h. Environment: prod dedicated pool in us-west serving gpt-x-2.7b-quant pinned model. Observed behavior: sudden rise in queued requests, many 429 and transient 5xx failures from internal allocator, and frequent short-lived GPU attach failures. Expected behavior: steady throughput within SLA for pinned capacity. This ticket captures support triage, initial hypotheses, telemetry extracts, and mitigation plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route steady traffic mimic for BrightCompose workload profile (mix of short chatlets and medium completions) to their dedicated pool in us-west.
2) During simulated midday peak, introduce a bursty background tenant that opens many short-lived multiplexed streams at 30ms interarrival for 5 minutes.
3) Observe autoscaler decisions, allocator attach logs, and per-GPU slot occupancy over the window.
4) Verify p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, and any 5xx/429 spikes from the serving runtime.

comments: 2026-03-13T11:20 Maya Chen (Support): Logged on behalf of BrightCompose. Customer reports throughput degradation starting ~11:00 UTC intermittently, affecting live gen routes. They see request spikes and then a slow recovery. Added traces and sample request IDs.

2026-03-13T11:35 Diego Alvarez (SRE): Confirmed cluster telemetry shows short windows of high attach-failure rate and multiple small-slot evictions. Opening investigation with allocator team. Assigning to Diego for deeper analysis.

2026-03-13T12:05 Lina R. (Allocator): Observed affinity churn for GPU 2-4; prefetched KV cache footprint increased transiently causing eviction pressure and slot fragmentation. Hypothesis: bursty short streams cause slot fragmentation and autoscaler mis-evaluates scale-in/out due to noisy telemetry.

2026-03-13T13:12 Maya Chen (Support): Customer ran a replay of yesterday's traffic; we saw repeated p99 spikes matching the windows described. Customer requested ETA for stabilization or a temporary workaround.
2026-03-13T14:00 Diego Alvarez (SRE): Temporary mitigation enacted: enable per-tenant attach backoff smoothing and raise allocator attach_retry window for BrightCompose pool. Monitoring impact.

2026-03-13T17:10 Diego Alvarez (SRE): After mitigation, observed two smaller incidents but no full throughput collapse. Continuing root-cause investigation and scheduling follow-up with autoscaler team.
investigation_notes: Telemetry: correlated spikes in 'attach_failure_rate' and 'slot_eviction_count' with short-stream fanout events; burst windows show KV-cache working set suddenly expands by ~28% triggering eviction waves.

Autoscaler behavior: evaluation function is sampling latency/queue metrics with a 30s window and has recently had parameter change to shorten smoothing window -> more sensitive to transient spikes, leading to oscillatory decisioning.

Allocator findings: slot fragmentation is high during incidents; many slots are held by ephemeral short-lived connections, preventing efficient batch packing and causing attach contention on remaining GPUs.

Hypothesis: noisy short-stream tenant (not BrightCompose) induces transient KV-cache growth + heartbeat bursts which cause evictions and allocator attach churn. Autoscaler then refrains from scaling due to the short sampling window and low aggregate 'score', leaving pinned pool understaffed to absorb the sudden tail.
Cross-checks: compared with SUP-712909 pattern (warmup lag) but distinct due to higher eviction counts and attach failure signature; linked for context.
resolution: Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-13 14:00 UTC): enabled per-tenant attach backoff smoothing for BrightCompose pool and increased attach_retry window to reduce attach churn. Also applied temporary throttle on ephemeral-tenant connection creation in us-west reserved hosts.
Observed effect: p99 latency reduced from 2.3s to ~420ms during subsequent bursts; full throughput largely recovered. Two smaller spikes still present but magnitude reduced.

Planned medium-term fixes: 1) Autoscaler parameter change to increase smoothing window to 60s during predicted high-noise windows; 2) Change allocator packing policy to prefer slot consolidation for dedicated pools (RFC in progress); 3) Add per-tenant burst detection metric to trigger temporary soft-quota for ephemeral tenants.

Owner and timeline: Autoscaler team (owner: Priya Nair) to deploy smoothing window change as A/B during low-risk window (ETA 3 days). Allocator team (owner: Lina R.) to prototype packing change (ETA 2 weeks). Support to coordinate customer communication and postmortem.
Post-incident follow-up: schedule 1:1 with BrightCompose to review patterns and confirm acceptable mitigation; collect more targeted traces for allocator repacking pilot.
next_steps: 1) Autoscaler A/B rollout: increase smoothing window and monitor false-positive scale decisions (owner: Priya, ETA: 72h).
2) Allocator packing RFC: prototype and run canary on non-prod, then staged rollout to dedicated pools (owner: Lina, ETA: 14 days).
3) Telemetry: add 'per-tenant short-stream rate' and 'kv-cache-delta' alert with 5m burn-in to detect precursor patterns earlier (owner: Observability, ETA: 5 days).
4) Customer comms: send interim incident summary and mitigation notes to BrightCompose (owner: Maya, ETA: today EOD).
